athenaeum_hadriani.name: Athenaeum of Hadrian (Piazza Venezia halls)
athenaeum_hadriani.summary: Three parallel halls with steep stepped seating found in 2008-2012 under Piazza Venezia during the Metro C works, identified with the Athenaeum that Hadrian founded for rhetoric and poetry recitals, beside the Forum of Trajan. In the 6th-7th century one hall housed a metal workshop.
scholarship: Egidi, Serlorenzi et al., excavation reports on Piazza Venezia (2010s)
Claridge, Rome: An Oxford Archaeological Guide (2nd ed., 2010)
athenaeum_hadriani.note: Location from Pleiades; orientation assumed parallel to the forum grid. Boundary building between districts.

pons_probi_v1.name: Pons Probi
pons_probi_v1.summary: Bridge built under Probus (276-282) below the Aventine, linking the Emporium and Marmorata with Transtiberim near the Porta Portuensis.
pons_probi_v1.note: Remains seen near the Marmorata (Via Marmorata / Arco di S. Lazzaro) and removed in 1484; crossing placed opposite them, about 180 m downstream of the modern Ponte Sublicio.

nymphaeum_of_egeria_v1.note: Position from the standing nymphaeum in the Valle della Caffarella (OSM node 259671299).

nemus_caesarum_a.note: A 40 m band around a basin of 1800 x 1200 Roman feet (533 x 355 m) assumed centred near S. Cosimato with the long side running NNW-SSE (345/165 deg), matching the naumachia_augusti_v1 pool; split into two L-shaped halves so each footprint is a simple polygon. Position and orientation of the basin are uncertain.

phases.t: Aqua Traiana opened; its terminal run descends the Janiculum
first excavated mill phases (early third century)

janiculum_mills_v1.note: Line of mills along the course of the aqueduct inside the Aurelian Wall near Porta Aurelia. The excavated mills under the American Academy and Via Garibaldi date from the early third century onward; from = 200 accordingly (begun = 109, the aqueduct).

temple_of_summanus_v1.summary: Temple of the god of nocturnal thunder near the Circus Maximus, dedicated during the war with Pyrrhus (c. 278 BC) after lightning struck the terracotta statue of Summanus on the pediment of the Capitoline temple of Jupiter and its head was found in the Tiber.

villa_publica_v2.summary: Rebuilt and enlarged by the censors of 194 BC; a coin of 59 BC shows a two-storey colonnaded building. Sulla had thousands of surrendered prisoners massacred here in 82 BC (8,000 in the Livian epitome; Plutarch gives 6,000 and says the circus) within earshot of the Senate, and Varro set his dialogue on farming here. It disappeared under Domitian's Divorum after the fire of 80.

terebinthus_neronis_v1.note: Position conjectural: placed north of the Via Cornelia some 170 m west of the Meta Romuli, toward the Naumachia and the Vatican, with which medieval sources associate it; form from Filarete and Cimabue's views.

san_marcello_v1.note: OSM footprint. The present church (16th century) faces east onto Via del Corso; the early basilica was oriented the other way, so its facade is set facing west (rot 254). The early church's orientation is debated.

The record follows the reading in its own note (Beltrami's transverse cella 43.8 x 19.8 m, with the Agrippan pronaos found in 1996-97 under the Hadrianic porch, facing north), but its centre lay 8 m north of the rotunda centre, i.e. entirely inside the later rotunda. Under that reading the cella lay beneath the Hadrianic intermediate block and porch and the pronaos under the porch, so the 40 m building is centred ~25 m further north.
log.source: Virgili and Battistelli excavations 1996-97 as summarised in La Rocca, in Marder and Wilson Jones (eds), The Pantheon (2015); Beltrami 1898

log.old: Temple of the god of nocturnal thunder, dedicated during the war with Pyrrhus near the Circus Maximus; its terracotta statue on the pediment was struck by lightning in 278 BC.
log.new: Temple of the god of nocturnal thunder near the Circus Maximus, dedicated during the war with Pyrrhus (c. 278 BC) after lightning struck the terracotta statue of Summanus on the pediment of the Capitoline temple of Jupiter and its head was found in the Tiber.
log.reason: The statue struck by lightning stood on the Capitoline temple, not on this temple; the strike preceded and prompted the foundation.

log.old: Rebuilt and enlarged by the censors of 194 BC; a coin of 59 BC shows a two-storey colonnaded building. Sulla had 6,000 prisoners massacred here in 82 BC within earshot of the Senate, and Varro set his dialogue on farming here. It disappeared under Domitian's Divorum after the fire of 80.
log.new: Rebuilt and enlarged by the censors of 194 BC; a coin of 59 BC shows a two-storey colonnaded building. Sulla had thousands of surrendered prisoners massacred here in 82 BC (8,000 in the Livian epitome; Plutarch gives 6,000 and says the circus) within earshot of the Senate, and Varro set his dialogue on farming here. It disappeared under Domitian's Divorum after the fire of 80.
log.reason: Plutarch (the only source cited) puts the massacre in the circus; the Villa Publica location comes from the Livian epitome.
Added the source that actually places Sulla's massacre in the Villa Publica.

log.old: Position between the Meta Romuli and the Mausoleum of Hadrian conjectural; form from Filarete and Cimabue's views.
log.new: Position conjectural: placed north of the Via Cornelia some 170 m west of the Meta Romuli, toward the Naumachia and the Vatican, with which medieval sources associate it; form from Filarete and Cimabue's views.
log.reason: The note said the tomb was placed between the Meta Romuli and the Mausoleum of Hadrian, but the coordinates put it west of the Meta, away from the Mausoleum.

log.old: OSM footprint; facade faces W to Via del Corso; the early church's orientation is debated.
log.new: OSM footprint. The present church (16th century) faces east onto Via del Corso; the early basilica was oriented the other way, so its facade is set facing west (rot 254). The early church's orientation is debated.
log.reason: The note said the facade faces west to Via del Corso, but the Corso lies east of the church; rot 254 is right only for the reversed early church.
log.source: OSM; c_3 record note (orientation reversed in the 16th century)
